    Camacho v. Army (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca13-26-01728 / USCOURTS-ca13-26-01728-0

    FAPD-AI: The Federal Circuit affirmed a Merit Systems Protection Board decision that denied Rosie Camacho's request for corrective action in her individual right of action appeal, which alleged retaliation against the Department of the Army for 14 protected disclosures. In this nonprecedential per curiam opinion, decided October 26, 2026, the court found no reversible error in the Board's discovery rulings or its application of the Carr factors under 5 U.S.C. § 1221(e). The court affirmed and awarded no costs. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 20:26:56 Eastern time ET
    C J Hesse Inc, et al v. American Family Home Insurance Co (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-03085 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-03085-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit affirmed a district court's grant of summary judgment to American Family Home Insurance Company in a suit by C.J. Hesse, Inc. and Atlantic Pier Co., Inc., who had argued the insurer owed a duty to defend them in six lawsuits arising from garbage truck accidents at a landfill. The court held that the garbage trucks were not covered autos under the commercial automobile policy, applying New Jersey law on policy interpretation and the duty to defend. This nonprecedential opinion was filed October 26, 2026. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca8-25-03000 / USCOURTS-ca8-25-03000-0

    FAPD-AI: The Eighth Circuit Clerk of Court sent a letter dated October 26, 2026, to counsel in Corner Post, Inc. v. Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, No. 25-3000, stating that the court issued an opinion and entered judgment that day. The letter reminds counsel that petitions for rehearing or rehearing en banc must be received within 45 days of the entry of judgment, must be filed electronically in CM/ECF, and are subject to denial as untimely if received late. Bondi, 606 U.S. 259 (2025), and assumed without deciding that the 30-day deadline in 8 U.S.C. § 1252(b)(1) may be equitably tolled.     Goodwin v. Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca13-26-01616 / USCOURTS-ca13-26-01616-0

    FAPD-AI: The Federal Circuit issued a nonprecedential per curiam decision affirming a Merit Systems Protection Board decision that denied Kiwanna Goodwin's request for corrective action under the Whistleblower Protection Act and the Whistleblower Protection Enhancement Act against the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation. The court found that substantial evidence supported the Board's finding that the agency showed by clear and convincing evidence it would have taken the same four personnel actions absent Goodwin's protected disclosures and activity. The personnel actions at issue were the termination of her supervisory appointment, a nondisclosure agreement, pay setting, and a performance rating. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca1-25-01034 / USCOURTS-ca1-25-01034-0

    FAPD-AI: In an opinion dated October 26, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit affirmed the District of Maine's grant of summary judgment to the non-signing spouse, Jackie L. Bowden, in a foreclosure action brought by U.S. Bank Trust, N.A. The court held that a notice under Me. Rev. Stat. Ann. tit. 14, § 6111 is required when a mortgage has matured, when the non-signing spouse holds a judicially determined interest subject to the mortgage, and when a prior foreclosure judgment was entered only against the signing spouse. The court concluded that the notice sent in May 2021 did not comply with the statutory requirements. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-125, the Clergy Act, allows ordained ministers, members of religious orders, and Christian Science practitioners who hold an exemption from Social Security coverage under section 1402(e)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code to revoke that exemption by filing an application with the Commissioner of Internal Revenue by the applicable tax return due date. Revocations take effect for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028, and applicants may not later re-elect the exemption. The Act also requires the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, in consultation with the Commissioner of Social Security, to submit to Congress within 90 days of enactment a plan to inform affected individuals of their eligibility to revoke the exemption.     Enacted law · govinfo API · PLAW-119publ127

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-127, the Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act, directs the Secretary of Commerce to study, within one year of enactment, products in each of the 16 critical infrastructure sectors that are in high demand and imported due to manufacturing, material, or supply chain constraints. The study is to analyze the costs, benefits, and effects on jobs and product prices of manufacturing those products in the United States, including in rural areas and industrial parks. The Secretary must submit a report with recommendations to Congress within 18 months of enactment and post it publicly on the Department of Commerce website, and the Act does not authorize the Secretary to compel information from any person. PLAW-SEL-01

    Public Law 119–129: To require online dating service providers to provide fraud ban notifications to online dating serv… (opens in a new tab)
    Enacted law · govinfo API · PLAW-119publ129

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-129, the Romance Scam Prevention Act, requires online dating service providers to send a fraud ban notification to any member who has received a message from a banned member, generally within 24 hours of the ban, with extensions at the provider's judgment or at a law enforcement official's request. Each notification must be clear and conspicuous, sent by email or text message, and include specified contents such as the banned member's profile identifier, a warning against sending cash or financial information, and provider contact information. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general may enforce the Act, and the Act preempts state laws that govern whether or how providers must give such notifications. The Act takes effect one year after enactment. PLAW-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-131, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, directs the Secretary of Labor to implement, within 180 days of enactment, a program of training and periodic continuing education for Department of Labor employees on detecting human trafficking and referring suspected cases. The training is to cover methods for identifying suspected victims and traffickers, a referral course of action to the Department of Justice and other authorities, and an evaluation of the training, with the Wage and Hour Division training considering states with significant increases in oppressive child labor. The Secretary must report annually to the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions on the training provided, its effectiveness, and the number of referred cases.     FAPD-AI: Public Law 119–134, cited as the "License to Drill Act," was approved October 20, 2026, and amends Section 35(d) of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 191(d)). The amendments replace references to 2026 with 2037 in paragraphs (1) and (4), extending the period during which the Secretary of the Interior is required to collect a fee for each new application for a permit to drill. Paragraph (3) is revised to direct the transfer, for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2037, of all fees collected under the subsection to the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund. PLAW-SEL-01

    Subsistence Management Regulations for Public Lands in Alaska—2026-27 and 2027-28 Subsistence Taking of Wildlife Regula… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE · FR-2026-10-27 / 2026-21849

    official summary: This final rule revises regulations for hunting and trapping seasons, harvest limits, and methods and means related to taking of wildlife for subsistence uses during the 2026-27 and 2027-28 regulatory years. The Federal Subsistence Board (hereafter referred to as “the Board”) is on a schedule of completing the process of revising subsistence taking of wildlife regulations in even-numbered years and subsistence taking of fish and shellfish regulations in odd-numbered years; public proposal and review processes take place during the preceding year. The Board also addresses customary and traditional use determinations during the applicable cycle. This final rule revises the existing subsistence wildlife taking regulations, the general regulations on subsistence taking of fish and wildlife, customary and traditional use determinations, and addresses a deferred proposal regarding eulachon harvest in District 1 from the last fish cycle and a deferred proposal regarding brown bear hide sales from the last wildlife cycle. This final rule also makes administrative corrections to the regulations and corrects errors discovered since the last rulemaking. FR-SEL-01

    Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-10-27 / 2026-21852

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an event involving a CFM Model CFM56-7B26/3 engine where a fan blade separated and resulted in an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) with debris penetrating the fuselage, which caused a loss of pressurization and prompted an emergency descent. This proposed AD would require a visual inspection of the fan blades for findings considered not serviceable and, depending on the results of the inspection, replacement with a serviceable part and additional fan blade inspections. This proposed AD would also require sending the inspection results to CFM if any finding considered not serviceable is found. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-10-27 / 2026-21854

    official summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model SA 365 N helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of tightening torque loss on the input flange nut due to circular wear on the faces of the flange, the slip ring, and the input flange. This condition, if not addressed, could lead to degradation or jamming of the input roller bearings and loss of yaw control of the helicopter. This AD requires repetitive functional inspections (checks) and, depending on the results of the inspections, corrective actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

This AD was prompted by reports of cracks on the cable drum of the rescue hoist assembly. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the cable drum of certain rescue hoist assemblies for cracks and, depending on the results, replacing or repairing the cable drum of the rescue hoist assembly. This AD also prohibits the operation and the installation of an affected rescue hoist assembly on a helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

This rule covers current and former Department of Justice employees and their dependents. FR-SEL-01
